messages.text: Western yodeling, cello suites, and the quiet rhythm of local transit

A cool, drizzly Thursday settles over Canton as we head toward the weekend. Today’s focus turns to the intersection of artistic performance and the practical realities of protecting our personal information.
Expect light drizzle throughout the day with a high of 41°F and a low of 30°F.
The sun rises at 7:22 AM and sets at 5:14 PM, with a 14.1% illuminated waxing crescent moon overhead.

For a thoughtful evening, catch the free performance by Duo Dolce featuring cello and piano at the Earl V. Moore Building in Ann Arbor at 8:00 PM, or hear the harmonies of Riders in the Sky at The Ark, also at 8:00 PM.
Community members are gathering tomorrow, November 14, at 9:00 AM for the United Way Make a Difference Day.

A Canton resident recently identified fraudulent medical billing in her name, highlighting the need for vigilance regarding insurance notices. Meanwhile, Plymouth is initiating a one-year pilot program using solar-powered cameras to help drivers monitor train crossing blockages at North Main Street.
Prepare for the United Way Make a Difference Day tomorrow morning to engage with local volunteer efforts.
Published 2026-11-11: Some PFAS chemicals are declining in English rivers but others are appearing.
